title: US Strikes Iran After Tanker Attacks in Strait of Hormuz; Three Ships Hit in 24 Hours
summary: The United States launched military strikes on Iran following attacks on British tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, with three ships struck within 24 hours. Washington described the strikes as a response to Iran's 'violation of truce'. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint through which approximately 20% of global oil trade passes, making the flare-up significant for global energy markets. India, which imports a substantial share of its crude oil from the Gulf region, faces direct economic exposure to any sustained conflict.
exam_angle: Strait of Hormuz is a critical maritime chokepoint relevant to GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy/Energy Security). US-Iran tensions, freedom of navigation, and India's energy import dependence are recurring UPSC themes.
key_facts: Strait of Hormuz: ~20% of global oil trade passes through it
US launched strikes on Iran citing 'violation of truce'
Three ships struck within 24 hours in the strait
India imports a major share of crude from Gulf region — energy security implication

title: Indonesia to Purchase BrahMos Missiles; PM Modi Addresses Indonesian Parliament
summary: Indonesia has agreed to purchase BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles from India, deepening defence ties between the two nations. PM Narendra Modi addressed the Indonesian Parliament (DPR) during his state visit to Jakarta, calling Indonesia a 'natural space partner' and offering satellite launch capabilities. Modi also invoked the 'next 25 years' as crucial for India-Indonesia partnership and reiterated India's dialogue-and-diplomacy stance in the context of global tensions. India also signed a pact with Indonesia for cooperation in minerals and technology of the steel supply chain.
exam_angle: BrahMos export signals India's emergence as a defence exporter — directly relevant to GS Paper 3 (Defence/Internal Security) and GS Paper 2 (IR/India's Neighbourhood & Beyond). Indonesia is part of ASEAN, central to India's Act East Policy.
key_facts: BrahMos: India-Russia joint venture supersonic cruise missile
Indonesia becomes a BrahMos buyer — supports India's defence export goals
PM Modi addressed Indonesian Parliament (DPR) during state visit to Jakarta
India-Indonesia pact signed on minerals and steel supply chain technology

title: PM Modi Addresses Indonesian Parliament: UNSC Reforms, Palestine Policy, Space Partnership
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, during his address to the Indonesian Parliament, called for inclusive development and reforms in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC). Modi reiterated India's long-standing support for a two-state solution on Palestine and called for an immediate ceasefire. He offered Indonesia satellite launch capabilities, describing Jakarta as India's 'natural space partner', and emphasised the deep bond between India, Indonesia, and the Indian Ocean region. India and Indonesia also signed a pact on minerals and steel supply chain cooperation.
exam_angle: India's UNSC reform demand, Act East Policy, and India-Indonesia civilisational ties are recurring GS Paper 2 themes. India's Palestine policy (two-state solution, UNGA votes) is frequently asked.
key_facts: India supports UNSC reforms — permanent membership demand
India reiterates two-state solution for Palestine; calls for immediate ceasefire
India offers Indonesia satellite launch capability — space diplomacy
India-Indonesia partnership termed crucial for 'next 25 years'
source: Times of India / The Hindu / News18

title: FDI Inflows to India Rose 44% to USD 39 Billion in 2025: UN Report
summary: According to a United Nations report, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows into India increased by 44% to USD 39 billion in 2025, reflecting growing investor confidence in the Indian economy. This makes India one of the top FDI destinations globally. PM Modi, addressing the Indian diaspora in Jakarta, stated that 'India's economy is driving global growth' and highlighted India's mantra of 'Reform, Perform and Transform'. India also urged the US to reconsider a proposed 12.5% tariff under USTR's Section 301 'forced labour' probe.
exam_angle: FDI data from UN/UNCTAD reports is directly asked in GS Paper 3 (Economy). India's trade disputes with the US under USTR Section 301 connect to WTO, trade policy, and bilateral economic relations.
key_facts: India FDI inflows: USD 39 billion in 2025 — up 44% YoY (UN report)
India urged US to withdraw proposed 12.5% tariff under USTR Section 301 'forced labour' probe
PM Modi: 'India is driving global growth'; mantra: Reform, Perform, Transform
Auto component industry pivoting to FTAs as US exports remain flat

title: E20 Petrol Rollout Faces Supreme Court Scrutiny; Government Defends Ethanol Blending
summary: A litigant before the Supreme Court alleged 'silent compulsion' in the E20 petrol rollout, claiming vehicle owners are being forced to use ethanol-blended fuel without adequate notification. Union Minister Hardeep Puri rejected claims of engine damage, stating that 'serviced vehicles are not facing difficulty'. India's ethanol blending programme targets 20% blending (E20) by 2025 under the National Biofuel Policy. The issue has political implications with reports suggesting it is impacting the BJP's electoral standing.
exam_angle: Ethanol blending is part of India's energy security and green fuel transition policy — GS Paper 3 (Economy/Environment). Supreme Court intervention on policy rollout connects to GS Paper 2 (Polity/Judiciary).
key_facts: E20 = 20% ethanol blended petrol; India's target under National Biofuel Policy 2018
Supreme Court hearing petition on 'silent compulsion' in E20 rollout
Minister Hardeep Puri: 'Serviced vehicles not facing difficulty'
E25 rethink also underway amid EV adoption challenges
source: Times of India / The Hindu / Indian Express

title: Lawrence Bishnoi Gang Charged in US with Ordering Hardeep Singh Nijjar's 2023 Murder
summary: US prosecutors have charged members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang with ordering the 2023 murder of Hardeep Singh Nijjar, a Canadian Sikh separatist, in British Columbia, Canada. The US indictment connects the Indian organised crime network to the assassination, which had previously triggered a major India-Canada diplomatic row. Separately, US prosecutors arrested 24 individuals in a major probe into India-based organised crime. An imprisoned Indian gang leader was specifically named in the charges.
exam_angle: India-Canada diplomatic tensions over Nijjar's killing, the Khalistan issue, and India's response to foreign interference are central to GS Paper 2 (IR). The US indictment internationalises the issue further.
key_facts: Hardeep Singh Nijjar murdered in June 2023 in Surrey, British Columbia, Canada
Lawrence Bishnoi gang named in US federal indictment
US arrested 24 individuals in probe into India-based organised crime
Issue triggered India-Canada diplomatic standoff in 2023

title: Trump Considers F-35 Sale to Turkey, Pledges to Lift Sanctions on Ankara
summary: US President Donald Trump, during his visit to Ankara, announced plans to lift sanctions on Turkey and said he would 'consider' selling F-35 stealth fighter jets to Türkiye. Israel's PM Benjamin Netanyahu publicly opposed the potential F-35 sale to Turkey. Turkey was originally removed from the F-35 programme in 2019 after it purchased Russia's S-400 air defence system, triggering US sanctions under CAATSA (Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act). The development has significant implications for NATO cohesion and West Asia geopolitics.
exam_angle: CAATSA is directly relevant as India also procured Russian S-400 systems and received a waiver — frequently asked in GS Paper 2 (IR). NATO solidarity, US-Turkey-Israel dynamics are important IR themes.
key_facts: Turkey removed from F-35 programme in 2019 after S-400 purchase from Russia
US sanctions on Turkey under CAATSA (Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act)
Trump pledges to lift sanctions on Türkiye and consider F-35 sale
India also procured S-400 from Russia and received CAATSA waiver

title: Wayanad on Red Alert as Landslide Kills 4, Leaves 6 Missing at Tunnel Site
summary: Wayanad district in Kerala has been placed on red alert after a landslide at a tunnel construction site killed at least 4 people and left 6 missing. Mumbai received a brief respite after two days of heavy rain, while orange alerts were issued for several Maharashtra districts. The incidents are part of the active 2026 Southwest Monsoon season, which has caused widespread flooding and landslides across India's western coast. AI-based early warning systems helped Maharashtra authorities prepare for cloudburst-like rains in Nashik.
exam_angle: Landslide-prone zones, monsoon disasters, and disaster management are recurring themes in GS Paper 1 (Geography) and GS Paper 3 (Disaster Management). AI use in disaster early warning is a GS Paper 3 Sci-Tech angle.
key_facts: Wayanad (Kerala) on red alert; 4 dead, 6 missing at tunnel construction site landslide
Wayanad suffered major landslide disaster in July 2024 as well — recurring vulnerability
AI-based early warning system used in Maharashtra's Nashik for cloudburst prediction
India Meteorological Department issues colour-coded alerts: Green, Yellow, Orange, Red

title: TribeX Digital Platform for Tribal Arts and Culture Launched by Union Tribal Affairs Ministry
summary: Union Tribal Affairs Minister Jual Oram launched TribeX, a digital learning platform dedicated to tribal arts, culture, and traditional knowledge. The platform aims to preserve and promote India's rich tribal heritage by providing a digital repository and learning resource accessible to tribal communities and researchers. The launch aligns with India's broader push for digital inclusion of marginalised communities and the preservation of intangible cultural heritage.
exam_angle: Government schemes for tribal welfare and digital inclusion are important for GS Paper 2 (Governance/Social Justice). Preservation of intangible cultural heritage connects to GS Paper 1 (Culture).
key_facts: Platform name: TribeX
Launched by: Union Tribal Affairs Minister Jual Oram
Focus: Digital learning for tribal arts, culture, and traditional knowledge
Ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs

title: DeepSeek's In-House Chip Development Rattles US Tech Stocks; Nasdaq Falls
summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek announced plans to develop in-house AI chips, sending shockwaves through global semiconductor markets. US chip stocks including Nvidia, Intel, AMD, Micron, and Sandisk fell by up to 14%. The Nasdaq index was set to open lower as investor confidence in US AI chip dominance wavered. DeepSeek had earlier made global headlines in early 2025 when its low-cost AI model challenged US AI supremacy, raising questions about export control effectiveness.
exam_angle: AI chip competition between the US and China, semiconductor export controls, and India's semiconductor mission are key GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Economy) themes. DeepSeek's emergence is a critical geopolitical technology story.
key_facts: DeepSeek (China) announced in-house AI chip development
Nvidia, Intel, AMD fell up to 14% on the news
US has imposed semiconductor export controls on China (CHIPS Act, BIS rules)
India has its own semiconductor mission — India Semiconductor Mission (ISM)

title: Bengaluru Startup's Surveillance Satellite Knocked Out by Solar Storm
summary: A surveillance satellite operated by a Bengaluru-based startup was knocked out by a solar storm (geomagnetic disturbance), the company confirmed. The startup announced it is working on a comeback, highlighting the vulnerability of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites to space weather events. Solar storms, caused by coronal mass ejections (CMEs) from the Sun, can damage satellite electronics and disrupt communications, GPS, and power grids. The incident underscores the importance of space weather monitoring for India's growing private space sector.
exam_angle: India's private space sector (IN-SPACe framework), solar storms and their effects, and LEO satellite vulnerability are important GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Space) topics.
key_facts: Solar storm (coronal mass ejection/CME) knocked out a Bengaluru startup's surveillance satellite
Geomagnetic storms can disrupt satellites, GPS, power grids, and HF radio
India's private space sector regulated under IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre)
Solar Cycle 25 (current cycle) has been more active than predicted

title: Government Directs EV Manufacturers to Strengthen Cybersecurity and Audit Battery Systems
summary: The Indian government has directed electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers to tighten cybersecurity protocols and conduct mandatory audits of battery management systems. The directive comes amid growing concerns about data security in connected vehicles and the safety of lithium-ion battery packs after several fire incidents. India's EV sector has been growing rapidly under the FAME scheme and PM E-Bus Sewa programme, making regulatory oversight increasingly important.
exam_angle: EV policy, battery safety, and cybersecurity in connected vehicles are relevant to GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Economy). FAME scheme and India's EV transition are standard topics.
key_facts: Govt directive to EV makers: tighten cybersecurity and audit battery management systems
Connected EVs are potential cybersecurity vulnerabilities
India's EV policy: FAME II scheme (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Electric Vehicles)
Battery fires in EVs have been a recurring safety concern in India since 2022

title: Ram Temple Board Overhauled After SIT Report on Donation Theft; Security Lapses Confirmed
summary: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teertha Kshetra Trust overhauled its board following an SIT (Special Investigation Team) report that confirmed theft of cash donations and serious security protocol failures at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. The SIT found that staff hired on a trust functionary's recommendations had stolen donations; six accused were identified. The Trust treasurer confirmed that valuable articles donated to the temple are safe and that over 30 kg of gold-like items are in the Trust's possession. The BBC reported the development as India's 'landmark Ram temple' undergoing significant reform.
exam_angle: The Ram Temple (consecrated January 2024) is a major cultural and constitutional landmark — connects to Article 25-28 (religious freedom), property rights of religious trusts, and governance of religious institutions.
key_facts: Trust: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teertha Kshetra Trust, Ayodhya
SIT report confirmed theft of donations and security protocol failures
Trust board overhauled after the report
Ram Temple consecrated on 22 January 2024 (Pran Pratishtha ceremony)

title: India-Indonesia Ink Pact on Minerals and Steel Supply Chain Technology
summary: India and Indonesia signed an agreement for cooperation in minerals and technology related to the steel supply chain during PM Modi's state visit to Jakarta. Indonesia is one of the world's largest producers of nickel, a critical mineral used in EV batteries and stainless steel, making the pact strategically important for India's energy transition and industrial goals. The agreement complements the BrahMos missile deal and broader defence-economic partnership announced during the visit.
exam_angle: Critical minerals diplomacy is a key GS Paper 3 (Economy) and GS Paper 2 (IR) theme. Indonesia's nickel reserves and India's need for critical minerals for EV batteries and green technology are important facts.
key_facts: India-Indonesia pact: cooperation in minerals and steel supply chain technology
Indonesia: world's largest nickel producer — critical for EV batteries
India's Critical Minerals Mission aims to secure supply of 30 critical minerals
Agreement signed during PM Modi's state visit to Jakarta, July 2026

title: PM Modi to Visit Australia After Indonesia; Human Rights Groups Plan Protests
summary: Following his state visit to Indonesia, PM Narendra Modi is set to visit Australia, where he is expected to receive a large diaspora welcome. However, human rights organisations plan protests over India's record on civil liberties and press freedom. India-Australia relations have deepened significantly since the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership signed in 2020, with defence, trade, and Quad cooperation as key pillars. The visit comes ahead of potential finalisation of the India-Australia Free Trade Agreement (ECTA) upgradation.
exam_angle: India-Australia bilateral relations, the Quad grouping, and India's diaspora diplomacy are standard GS Paper 2 (IR) topics. ECTA (Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement) is a key trade policy fact.
key_facts: India-Australia: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (2020)
Both are Quad members (India, US, Australia, Japan)
India-Australia ECTA (Interim FTA) signed April 2022
Modi visit: diaspora outreach and strategic bilateral agenda

title: Mumbai High Court: City Flooding 'Our Own Creation'; Cautions Against Blaming Civic Body
summary: The Bombay High Court observed that Mumbai's recurring flooding is largely 'our own creation', cautioning petitioners against solely blaming the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC). The Court's remarks came amid heavy monsoon-related flooding in the city, with waterlogging affecting large parts of Mumbai. The observation highlights judicial concern over unplanned urbanisation, encroachment of natural drainage systems, and inadequate urban planning as root causes of flood vulnerability in India's financial capital.
exam_angle: Urban flooding, judicial activism on urban governance, and the role of municipal bodies connect to GS Paper 2 (Polity/Governance) and GS Paper 1 (Geography/Disaster Management).
key_facts: Bombay High Court: Mumbai flooding is 'our own creation' — not solely BMC's fault
BMC (Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation): India's richest municipal body
Urban flooding linked to encroachment of Mithi River, Aarey, Mangroves
74th Constitutional Amendment: Urban Local Bodies' responsibilities include urban planning
